newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Sao Paulo bankruptcy filings up 41.9 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Sao Paulo bankruptcy filings up 41.9 pct in 1996.

text.p: Bankruptcy filings in the city of Sao Paulo totalled 14,417 in 1996, a rise of 41.9 percent over 1995, Sao Paulo Commerce Association (ACSP) said in a statement.
December bankruptcy filings, however, fell 29.1 percent to 942 when compared with the same month of 1995, ACSP said.

Sao Paulo Commerce Association also said consumer defaults, measured by the number of reported payment in arrears for over 30 days, fell a slight 3.2 percent in 1996 against the previous year, showing that "consumer bankruptcies remained at high levels" last year.
In December, consumer defaults fell 4.8 percent against November, reflecting retailer caution during the Christmas season when demand for credit traditionally rises, it said.
Consumer insolvencies, however, rose 46.8 percent over the same month of 1995, it added.
Regarding credit sales, ACSP noted a rise of 30.7 percent last year over 1995.
